featured_reviews.name: Neel
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to Zen Bowl for lunch to try their food, as I had heard they serve both South Indian and Chinese dishes. My visit was good overall, though not everything was perfect.

When I reached the restaurant, the staff greeted me in a polite way. The place looked clean and comfortable. The menu has many choices, so it is nice if you are going with friends or family who like different types of food.

To start my meal, I ordered a dosa and medu vada. The dosa was crispy and light brown, with a potato filling inside. It was fresh and not very oily. The medu vada was soft and warm, but a little heavy. They served both items with coconut chutney and sambar. The chutney tasted fresh and the sambar was mild. I liked these dishes, but they were not as tasty as what you get in a pure South Indian restaurant. Still, it was good enough for a mixed menu place.

After that, I tried their Chinese food. I ordered vegetable fried rice, Manchurian gravy, and chicken fried rice. The vegetable fried rice had good flavor and plenty of fresh vegetables. It was not too oily, which I liked. The Manchurian was my favorite dish. The sauce was tasty, with a little sweetness and spice, and the vegetable balls were crispy on the outside. The chicken fried rice was also nice, with soft rice and pieces of chicken. The chicken could have had a little more flavor, but it was still enjoyable.

One thing I liked about Zen Bowl is that they have food for both vegetarians and non-vegetarians. This makes it easy if you are eating with people who have different food choices. The portions were big enough, and the prices were fair. You get good value for your money here.

The service was friendly, but it was a bit slow. Even though the restaurant was not very crowded, I waited about 10–15 minutes for my food to arrive. The staff were polite and helpful once the food came, but faster service would have made the experience better.

The overall atmosphere was nice. It is a simple place where you can sit comfortably and have a relaxed meal. If you want a fancy restaurant, this may not be the right spot. But if you just want good food at a fair price, Zen Bowl is a decent choice.

I am giving Zen Bowl three stars because the food was fresh and tasty, but nothing was very special or unique. Some dishes were better than others. The Chinese items were definitely the best part of the meal.

featured_reviews.name: Franklin Paul
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Hidden Gem in Wadala Antophill– . Truly Delivers Excellence!

From the moment I stepped into Zen Bowl, I knew I was in for something special. The ambiance radiates warmth and care, but what truly sets this place apart is their uncompromising commitment to quality. Every dish is a celebration of flavor — fresh, wholesome, and most importantly, completely free from additives and preservatives. It’s rare to find a place where you can taste the authenticity in every bite.

And let me highlight what makes Zen bowl truly iconic: Entail. Without a doubt, it’s the best you’ll find anywhere in Wadala Antophill . A must-try dishes that defines the culinary excellence this restaurant stands for.

If you’re in Wadala Antophill and appreciate real food crafted with integrity and served with heart — Zen bowl is the place to be

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Kartik Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gypsy corner:
This has been my go to place since 7-8 years now. I have tried every single item on their menu right from the regulars to the specials and also the rarer festival specific ones.
Come here for an authentic and wholesome maharashtrian food experience. They have a wide menu from all day breakfast items to chats, pavbhaji and bhakri bhaji. Staple bhaji available daily are zunka, pithla, bharit and bharleli vangi apart from daily special bhaji. Choose any one with tandalachi/jowar bhakri and you have a meal at your hands with thecha and kanda. Top it off with varan bhat ani tup plate. If you get chance to come on Chaturthi or during Ganesh festival, do not miss their Ukdiche modak.
This place is love and comfort and same time. All servers are so kind and lovely that you feel like coming back again and again. Never do they ever forget to smile and greet their regulars(me). Catching one odd glimpse of some Marathi celeb here is not that uncommon too, so keep your cameras handy everyone. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.review_text:
very disappointing experience at Gypsy Restaurant, Dadar. When the restaurant gets crowded, the staff seem to rush the service and bring dishes without proper attention to quality.
The food was below average. The Chicken Lollipop was over-fried. The soup was completely bland and lacked any flavor.
What was even more frustrating was the service charge issue. When I asked for a breakup or explanation of the service charge added to the bill, none of the staff members could provide a clear answer. Eventually, the bill was settled after removing the service charge.
To make matters worse, while processing the card payment, the staff still asked for a tip. When I declined, they suggested that they could remove the service charge and take a tip instead, which felt highly unprofessional.
Overall, a very poor dining experience. I would not recommend this restaurant and would advise others to avoid it.

featured_reviews.name: Bahubali
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a fan of bold flavors and comforting Indo-Chinese food, this restaurant is definitely worth a visit. The menu offers a wide variety of classic Indian Chinese dishes, from crispy starters to flavorful gravies and perfectly cooked noodles and rice.
The taste stands out—well-balanced spices, fresh ingredients, and generous portions make every dish satisfying. Popular items like Manchurian, Hakka noodles, and fried rice are cooked just right, with authentic street-style flavors that Indian Chinese lovers appreciate.
The ambience is clean and pleasant, suitable for both family dining and casual outings with friends. Service is prompt and staff are polite, ensuring a smooth dining experience even during peak hours.
Overall, this restaurant offers great value for money, consistent taste, and a comforting Indian Chinese experience. Highly recommended for anyone craving delicious Indo-Chinese food.

Chicken Malai Tikka (3/5): The flavor was nice and well-marinated, but the chicken wasn’t as soft and tender as expected.

Chicken Nalli Nihari (3/5): The gravy tasted good and rich, but unfortunately the bone marrow pieces had a slightly weird smell and taste, which affected the overall experience.

Khameri Roti (2/5): Quite disappointing and not up to the mark.

Mutton Biryani (3/5): Very heavy on masala with lots of mixed flavors — decent, but a bit overwhelming.

Overall, an average dining experience that could be improved in terms of quality consistency and ambience.

featured_reviews.name: NAFIS AHMED
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Must-Visit for Nihari Lovers on Mohammed Ali Road!!
Chinese and Grill Nalli Nihari on Mohammed Ali Road is an absolute delight for food lovers. The Nalli Nihari is the true star—rich, aromatic, slow-cooked to perfection, and bursting with deep, authentic flavors. The meat is incredibly tender and the gravy is thick, soulful, and perfectly spiced, making every bite satisfying.
The other items are equally impressive, fresh, well-cooked, and generously portioned. Despite the rush that Mohammed Ali Road is known for, the service is quick and well-managed, and the staff is polite and attentive.
Hygiene is maintained well, prices are reasonable for the quality and quantity, and the overall experience feels truly worth it. If you’re exploring Mohammed Ali Road and craving hearty, flavorful non-veg food, this place should definitely be on your list. Highly recommended!!!

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Chinese Palace is one of the older Chinese restaurants in Mumbai, reportedly around since 1972. The location, however, can be slightly tricky to find, as it is situated on the second floor of a building and set a bit inside from the main road.

We visited as a large group of over 10 people for dinner, which gave us a good opportunity to sample a range of dishes from their extensive menu.

For starters, we ordered Crispy Thai Chicken and Crackling Spinach with Chicken, along with Sweet Corn Chicken Soup. For the mains, we went with Chicken Schezwan Fried Rice, Diced Chicken Chilli, and Stewed Wantons.

The food overall was tasty, though somewhat inconsistent across dishes. The soup was good, and among the starters, both the Crispy Thai Chicken and Crackling Spinach with Chicken stood out as particularly enjoyable. However, some items like the stewed wantons and the diced chicken chilli felt a bit on the blander side, and even the Schezwan fried rice lacked the expected punch.

Portions were generous, which worked well for a group setting. They also serve kimchi as a salad accompaniment, which was a slightly unusual but interesting touch.

Service was good in terms of staff behavior, but the preparation and delivery of food did take time, especially noticeable with a larger group.

Overall, Chinese Palace offers decent food with some standout dishes, but also a fair bit of inconsistency. Worth a visit for select items, but with a bit of patience required.

featured_reviews.name: Olivia Gomes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ming China – A Family Favourite Revisited
A restaurant close to our hearts, Ming China has moved from the bustling lanes of Mazagon to Wadi Bunder. We truly missed their cuisine, so a revisit was inevitable  and it did not disappoint.
We were greeted by warm, familiar faces who genuinely enquired about our well-being, instantly making us feel at home. We were escorted to a comfortable seating area, and the beautifully renovated space struck the perfect balance between nostalgic charm and modern elegance.
We ordered many of our all-time favourites, and every dish lived up to our expectations. While waiting, we were served a delicious khimchi ,a thoughtful and tasty touch.
The seafood soup was rich and flavourful, generously packed with shreds and chunks of prawns and crab ,a solid 10/10. Fresh lime sodas added a refreshing balance to the meal.
The Chicken Hakka Fingers are an absolute must-try  crisp, flavourful, and a clear 10/10.
The Chicken Lollipop in Shanghai Sauce truly elevated our taste buds  an 11/10, if that’s possible!😜
The Prawn Black Pepper & Salt, recommended by the staff, was well-cooked and delicious  8/10.
The Veggie Stir Fry was light, crunchy, refreshing, and a comforting accompaniment  8/10.
The Chicken Steamed Dumplings were melt-in-the-mouth perfection, paired beautifully with the sauces 10/10.
The portions were so generous that we couldn’t even make it to the main course.We  left happily  and completely satiated
If you’re looking for a warm, comfortable family dining experience, Ming China is highly recommended.
Great seating. Exceptional staff. Delicious food. A place worth returning to.
In case you are lucky you might even meet the owner a wonderful person down to earth and always with a warm smile

featured_reviews.review_text: The food here is good no doubt about it. But it didn't blow my mind away. Maybe it's me having placed serious hype on it. Standard tandoori roti not butter roti.
